review.brief_reason: The rewrite merges the denominator's four square roots sqrt(A)*sqrt(B)*sqrt(C)*sqrt(D) into a single sqrt(A*B*C*D). Each radicand is strictly positive for all real inputs: A >= 1 (the inner fraction is nonnegative and its denominator >= 1, with cos(cos(.)) bounded in [cos(1),1] hence never zero), B >= 1, C >= 1, D >= 1. Thus sqrt(a)sqrt(b)=sqrt(ab) holds exactly on the entire real domain, the common domain is all of R^4 for both expressions (no domain change), variable-to-column mapping and operator semantics are unchanged, and replacing four sqrt nodes with one is strictly simpler. Any floating-point discrepancy is at ulp scale, far below rel_tol=1e-6.
